page.overview:
What is Pokémon Red and Blue?

Pokémon Red Version and Pokémon Blue Version, commonly shortened as Pokémon Red and Blue, are Generation I games and the first two international Pokémon installments, released on September 28, 1998 for the Game Boy. In Japan, the original pair were Pocket Monsters Red and Green, which were then followed by the enhanced version, Pocket Monsters Blue, each released two years prior. Pokémon Yellow, a special edition which was based upon the anime series, would later be released internationally in 1999. Red and Blue in particular used the main code and script of Pocket Monsters Blue, but the wild Pokémon encounter data is based on the Japanese Red and Green, respectively.

Internationally, the games were referred to as "Pokémon", as it is a Romanized contraction of the Japanese brand, "Poketto Monsutā" (Pocket Monsters).

The version mascots of the games are Charizard and Blastoise, respectively.

Red and Blue were an instant hit in the West during release, selling 11.27 million copies and had established Pokémon as a whole into a worldwide phenomenon. It is currently considered one of the greatest and most influential RPG video games of all-time.
